title: Probe diary: sprintlet caching/batching ledger
content:
Purpose:
Quick, personal mini-sheet to track short experiments on prefix/KV cache behavior + small-batch effects for medium-length sequences. Not official experiment — notes-to-self style.

Hypotheses:
- Enabling prefix cache aggressively should reduce p95 for repeated-session workflows by ~20-40% for 1k+ token sequences.
- Small increases in batch_size (1->4) will reduce per-token cost but may increase cold-start p95.
- Quantized 8-bit path reduces GPU memory pressure but may slightly increase per-token latency for long sequences.

Notes on measurement:
- p95 measured across 200 requests per run; simulated session affinity by reusing session_id for 30% of requests.
- cost_est_usd = (tokens_generated * unit_usd_per_token). unit_usd_per_token set to $0.0000125 for quick calc (hosted estimate).
- model config shorthand: gpt-small-q8 (8-bit), gpt-small-fp16.
- cache_policy: none | prefix-only | aggressive-kv (prefix + KV reuse).

Quick run ledger (rows are compact):
run_id, date, model, quant, batch_size, cache_policy, avg_lat_ms, p95_lat_ms, tokens_generated, cost_est_usd, notes
R-2024-11-20-a, 2024-11-20, gpt-small, fp16, 1, none, 98, 180, 12, 0.00015, cold-start heavy, no session reuse
R-2024-11-20-b, 2024-11-20, gpt-small, fp16, 1, prefix-only, 82, 140, 12, 0.00015, prefix cache helped p95 by ~22%
R-2024-11-20-c, 2024-11-21, gpt-small, q8, 1, prefix-only, 90, 150, 12, 0.00015, q8 added ~8ms avg
R-2024-11-22-a, 2024-11-22, gpt-small, fp16, 4, prefix-only, 72, 130, 48, 0.00060, batch win: tokens/sec up, lower unit latency
R-2024-11-22-b, 2024-11-22, gpt-small, fp16, 4, aggressive-kv, 68, 115, 48, 0.00060, KV reuse reduced p95 further, jitter reduced
R-2024-11-25-a, 2024-11-25, gpt-small, q8, 8, aggressive-kv, 66, 108, 96, 0.00120, memory headroom good, slight avg latency improvement over fp16 at high batch

Observations / raw impressions:
- Prefix-only cache gives biggest single-step p95 improvement when session reuse >=25%. If session reuse low, overhead of cache lookup can offset benefits for tiny batches.
- Aggressive KV policy shines when batch_size >=4 and sequence length >800 tokens.
- Q8 path is worth exploring more at high batch: memory savings enable larger batches which offset slight per-token cost.
- p95 is noisy for runs under 200 requests; increase sample size for final numbers.

Questions to answer next sprint:
- How does cache eviction/window size affect tail latency for sequences with many unique prefixes?
- Does model sharding change effective cache hit rate (because different shards hold different KV slices)?
- At what batch threshold does batching hurt single-request latency unacceptably for host-tier SLOs?

To-do (short):
- [ ] Re-run R-2024-11-22-a/b with 1000 requests and 3 different session_reuse ratios (10%,30%,60%).
- [ ] Add simple chart: p95 vs batch_size for prefix-only vs aggressive-kv.
- [ ] Add cleanup script to compute cost_est_usd from real billing.csv (quick import).
- [ ] Confirm unit_usd_per_token with finance (linked JIRA).

Scratch notes (shorthand):
- warmup: 5 initial dummy calls to populate caches before measurement.
- set env LOG_HTTP=1 for request-level traces when debugging a surprising p95 spike.
- consider measuring p99 for canary runs; p95 masks tail-outlier regressions.

Quick bookmarks:
- design doc for cache: confluence.redwood/cache-design (local ref)
- PR that touched batching heuristics: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/834

End of mini-sheet. Keep in top of personal drive until solid numbers.
